text:
anya: heads-up — gpunode-12 had 5 OOMs between 02:12-02:40 UTC, kernel-selector flipped a few times and KV eviction raced but we still hit OOM on large-batched requests. noticed spike correlated with a long prompt arrival pattern. TL;DR: need a short emergency cheat-sheet for on-call to run immediate mitigations.

matt: ouch. any core dumps or profiler traces?

anya: got a short perf dump from the runtime profiler, attaching the query (saved to s3). main findings: kernel A (fast) consumes much more workspace than kernel B for long sequences; batching heuristic kept growing batch size to 48 due to concurrent small requests merged, pushing workspace > available. KV cache hit-rate drops during spikes -> coldstart evictions made things worse.

devon: can you paste the profiler lines? a few sample numbers help.

anya: paste from profiler: ```
seq_len P95: 1024
batch_size P95: 36
kernel_A_workspace: 6.4GB
kernel_B_workspace: 2.1GB
GPU free pre-oom: 400MB
KV_cache_size: fluctuating 1.2GB -> 0.3GB on eviction
```

luis: immediate mitigations i usually run: 1) pin kernel selector to kernel_B for this node pool 2) enforce batch_size cap of 16 via route config 3) enable strict KV TTL (30s) to free prefix cache 4) enable soft-fallback to smaller model variant for requests >512 tokens.

anya: putting a minimal checklist below we can share with on-call. trying to keep commands safe.

ops-bot: deploy-checklist created: infra/oom-mitigation/2419876543 - please confirm steps run and reactions.

matt: quick commands: ```bash
# pin kernel selector for node gpunode-12 pool
redwoodctl runtime patch kernel-selector --pool=gpunode-12 --force kernel_B
# cap batching at route level (example route id: /v1/generate)
redwoodctl routes update /v1/generate --max-batch=16
# KV TTL override for pool
redwoodctl config set kv.cache.ttl --pool=gpunode-12 30s
# route param to reject long requests
redwoodctl routes update /v1/generate --max-tokens=512
```

sre-elena: add circuit-breaker toggle too — temporarily flip request_shaper to "aggressive" so we can fail fast on heavy requests rather than let them queue: 
```yaml
request_shaper:
  mode: aggressive
  queue_limit: 8
  per_route_limit:
    - route: /v1/generate
      max_inflight: 2
```

devon: also watch allocator retry/backoff flags — if allocator is attempting infinite retries it holds workspace and starves others. set `gpu.allocator.max_retries=3` and `allocator.retry_backoff=100ms` for the hot pool.

luis: what about KV eviction policy? we can change to cost-aware eviction so long sequences that occupy lots of KV are evicted first. command: `redwoodctl config set kv.eviction_policy cost_aware`

anya: realtime dashboard checks for on-call: - GPU free < 1GB? escalate and pin kernels - KV hitrate < 20% and eviction spike? apply TTL override - Batch growth > 24? cap batch size - Latency tail spikes > 95th? flip to aggressive shaper - If node has repeated OOMs after config changes: cordon and migrate workloads 

matt: migration command if needed: `kubectl cordon gpunode-12 && drain --ignore-daemonsets` (we have runbooks for safe draining).

ops-bot: incident annotated: /incidents/2419876543/annotations - actions: kernel_pin, batch_cap, kv_ttl, shaper_toggle.

sre-elena: post-incident followups we should add to backlog: 1) adaptive batching cap that uses live workspace telemetry 2) kernel workspace profiling per model to prefer low-workspace kernels for long-seq routes 3) KV prefetch backpressure when eviction rate > x 4) improve allocator rejection contract (fast fail vs retry)

luis: i can take kernel profiling (2) — will produce a small matrix that maps model+seq_len -> recommended kernel and workspace estimate.

anya: devon do you want to own the adaptive batching task? it'll need runtime + router changes.

devon: yes, I'll take it. will sketch an API for soft caps and telemetry-driven caps.

matt: for on-call we should make a one-click toggle in console for "emergency low-workspace mode" that applies the above four mitigations. can UX/infra sync later.

anya: agreed — immediate step for on-call now: run matt's commands, flip shaper config, watch telemetry 10 min, escalate if OOM persists. ping me if anything weird. :thumbsup:

sre-elena: thanks team — i'll update the incident ticket with this cheat-sheet and post a short after-action tomorrow.

ops-bot: reminder scheduled: incident follow-up in 24h (owner: sre-elena).
